title: Values and Equality
summary: Primitive types, typeof, == versus ===, truthy and falsy, null and undefined.

steps.title: Primitive types
body: JavaScript has a small set of primitive types:
`typeof` tells you the type at run time:
console.log(typeof null);      // object  (a famous, permanent bug)

steps.explain: A variable declared without a value holds `undefined`. Both `1.5` and `"1.5"` keep their own types.

steps.title: == versus ===
body: - `===` (**strict**) is true only when both type and value match. This is what C# `==` does for primitives.
- `==` (**loose**) converts the types first, with surprising rules:

**Always use `===` and `!==`.** The one common exception some teams allow is `x == null`, which is true for both `null` and `undefined`. TypeScript also flags many loose comparisons between unrelated types as errors.

steps.prompt: Does each comparison evaluate to `true` or `false`?
steps.explain: Loose `==` converts types. Strict `===` does not. `NaN` is never equal to anything, even itself.

steps.title: Truthy and falsy
body: In C# an `if` needs a `bool`. In JavaScript any value works: it is converted to true or false.
The **falsy** values are exactly: `false`, `0`, `-0`, `0n`, `""`, `null`, `undefined`, `NaN`. Everything else is **truthy**, including `"0"`, `"false"`, `[]` and `{}`.
- `a || b` gives `a` if it is truthy, otherwise `b`.
- `a ?? b` gives `a` unless it is `null` or `undefined` (same as C# `??`).
console.log(qty || 10);   // 10  (0 is falsy: probably a bug!)
Optional chaining `user?.address?.city` works like C#: it stops at `null`/`undefined` and gives `undefined`.

steps.accept: `||` replaces every falsy value, so `0` and `""` get replaced. `??` replaces only `null` and `undefined`, so the real values `0` and `""` survive (the second line ends with an empty string).

steps.prompt: A settings object may have `retries: 0`, meaning "never retry". Which expression gives 3 only when `retries` was not set at all?
steps.explain: Only `??` treats `0` as a real value. The others all turn `0` into 3.

steps.title: Describe a value
prompt: - `"empty"` when it is the empty string `""`
`describe(0)` is `"number"`, not `"missing"`: zero is a real value.
hints: `if (!value)` would be wrong here: it also catches `0` and `false`.
